Subject: Custom SLA ask: uptime + latency commitments for enterprise deployment

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looks promising. We're heading into procurement and legal review and need a clear path for a custom SLA addendum that will sit as an exhibit to our MSA/SOW. A few specific asks from our side: 

- Availability: targeted 99.99% regional uptime (primary region) with defined measurement window and credit schedule for missed SLOs.
- Latency: P95 inference latency target of <150ms for text-generation endpoints, with agreed measurement methodology (tokenization, input size bucket).
- Exceptions: carve-outs for scheduled maintenance, force majeure, and planned model upgrades with a notice/maintenance window.
- Evidence: SOC2 report, telemetry sample for a 30-day burst window, and runbook for failover/testing.

Can you share initial order form wording we can circulate internally (procurement + legal) and an evidence checklist? Also flag anything you need from us (e.g., traffic profiles, P95 test queries, or IP allowlist details).

We'd like to understand implementation cadence (how long to onboard the annex) and whether Dedicated/Private deployment influences the commitments.

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara — thanks, and great questions. I put together an initial draft of order-form/annex language that maps to each of your bullets and an evidence checklist that should help procurement/legal move faster. Draft attached: redwood-sla-draft-v1.docx.

Quick summary / what I need from you:
- Confirm the primary region (us-west vs us-east) and whether you'd require multi-region failover as part of the annex.
- Share a sample traffic profile (QPS, average tokens per request, % of requests that are streaming) — we use that to size Dedicated capacity and to validate the latency measurement buckets.
- Let us know if Helix wants an initial 30-day performance verification (we can run a P95 test with your queries; that'll be in the evidence package).

Notes about deployment types:
- Hosted: we can commit to a regional uptime target and measurement but will include fallback language for cross-region failover if capacity is constrained.
- Dedicated/Private: commitments become more prescriptive (we can enforce capacity reservation and a higher availability guarantee) — there will be operational on-call and change management attachments.

I've looped in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (serving ops) to review the language and confirm any operational constraints or evidence gaps. Expect internal redlines within 48 hours.

Next step — I'll follow up with a proposed timeline and DocuSign route once legal signs off on the wording.

Thanks,
Jordan

Sara / Procurement team — thanks for the clear ask and for reviewing the draft. Per our internal review we've made a few conservative edits to protect both parties while keeping commercial intent:

- Measurement and credits: we set a single standardized measurement window (monthly UTC calendar month) and included a graduated credit schedule capped at 6 months of monthly service fees. We also added an audit-rights clause so customers can request measurement logs for a specific incident within 30 days.
- Latency verification: added explicit test harness definition (input sample set, traffic replay instructions, tokenization rules) and an initial 30-day verification period that will be used as a baseline for any latency claims.
- Exceptions & maintenance: clarified that scheduled maintenance with advance notice is excluded and added force majeure with an explicit escalation path.
- Liability: tied SLA credits to the order form only (no expansion of MSA indemnity/liability beyond existing MSA terms).

Next steps: Jordan to send the redlined doc via DocuSign (we will include an execution page for the SLA exhibit). Marissa / Ops will attach the telemetry report and the verification test results as an appendix to the exhibit.

DocuSign preparatory link (placeholder): https://docusign.example.com/placeholder/HP-SLA-EXH-2025
